name: Samuel Okafor, Cardiac Step-Down: DKA precipitated by a silent NSTEMI, hypokalemia on insulin, PCI

caseMeta.title: Cardiac step-down unit: DKA precipitated by a silent NSTEMI in a 45-year-old with type 1 diabetes: potassium 3.3 with the insulin held and ventricular ectopy, heparin, early invasive strategy with a drug-eluting stent, dual antiplatelet therapy, a radial-site hematoma, nicotine withdrawal and a commercial driver license at stake (3 days, checkpoints at every 0700 and 1900)
caseMeta.studentLevel: BSN / ADN medical-surgical and telemetry (upper level)
learningObjectives: Recognize DKA triggered by an acute coronary syndrome (epigastric ache, ST depression, rising troponin) and apply the adult protocol with a cardiac potassium goal of 4.0 or higher: insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h without a bolus, dextrose and 0.05 unit/kg/h once the glucose is under 250, and the resolution criteria (BHB under 0.6 plus venous pH 7.3 or higher or bicarbonate 18 or higher).

Apply the peripheral potassium rule when the potassium falls to 3.3 with PVCs on insulin: hold the insulin, KCl 10 mEq/100 mL riders one at a time (never more than 10 mEq/h from all sources, potassium-free carrier while a rider runs), restart only at 3.5 or higher with prescriber confirmation, and give glargine 2 hours before the drip stops.

Safely manage NSTEMI care: weight-based heparin with the 4,000-unit bolus and 1,000 units/h maximums and anti-Xa checks, nitroglycerin parameters, beta-blocker hold parameters, a fluid ceiling for an ischemic ventricle, pre-cath and contrast-kidney precautions, dual antiplatelet therapy, and right radial band and hematoma care.

Educate a person with type 1 diabetes and a new stent: sick-day rules (never omit basal insulin), atypical ischemia in diabetes, stent protection and bleeding precautions, nicotine replacement, hypoglycemia on a beta-blocker, and the commercial driver license pathway.

problems.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis precipitated by an NSTEMI (type 1 diabetes, 31 years)
problems.details: Glucose 540, venous pH 7.21, bicarbonate 12, anion gap 24, BHB 5.8 at 0140; corrected sodium 138.0. He skipped his mealtime lispro and his bedtime glargine 24 units because of nausea. Insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h = 8 units/h from 0215 (no bolus); hourly POC glucose. Resolves only with BHB under 0.6 plus venous pH 7.3 or higher or bicarbonate 18 or higher.

problems.name: NSTEMI (silent presentation: epigastric ache and fatigue; diabetic autonomic neuropathy)
problems.details: hs-troponin I 185 then 640 ng/L; 1.5 mm horizontal ST depression V4-V6 with T inversion V5-V6. Aspirin 324 mg given; heparin (4,000 unit bolus, 960 units/h; anti-Xa 0.30-0.70); atorvastatin 80 mg. Cardiology: early invasive strategy; beta-blocker deferred while volume-depleted. IV fluid ceiling 150 mL/h. Goal potassium 4.0-5.0.

orders.name: Full Code (wife Grace Okafor is the emergency contact)
Establish two peripheral IVs in the ED (18 gauge, left forearm and right antecubital; no central line). Assess every site hourly during infusions; remove when no longer needed
orders.instructions: Heparin runs alone on the right antecubital IV; the left forearm IV carries the carrier fluid, the insulin and, later, the potassium riders, each on its own pump channel. After the right radial catheterization no blood pressure cuff, venipuncture or IV on the right arm. Priming volume is discarded and not counted as intake.

orders.name: Continuous 5-lead ST-segment telemetry (V5 and lead II) through discharge; vital signs every hour while on the insulin infusion, then every 4 hours; strict intake and output with every void measured (urinal, no catheter); hourly urine while on the insulin infusion
orders.instructions: Notify for chest or epigastric pain, new ST change or ectopy, urine under 40 mL/h for 2 hours, new crackles or oxygen need, glucose under 150 on the infusion, or any infusion-site injury.

orders.name: ECG 12-lead now (epigastric ache with diaphoresis and nausea in a man with type 1 diabetes); acquire 0140, interpretation released 0150

Initial labs (ED) at 0140: venous blood gas, BMP, magnesium, phosphorus, beta-hydroxybutyrate, hs-troponin I, hepatic panel, lipid panel, CBC, HbA1c; urinalysis. Repeat chemistry, venous gas, BHB, magnesium, phosphorus and hs-troponin I at 0430 and again with the 0700 panel (troponin not repeated at 0700). POC glucose hourly from the insulin start
orders.instructions: Results are released 20-30 minutes after collection. Draw from an arm without an infusion running.

orders.name: 0.9% sodium chloride 1,000 mL bolus (ED)
orders.frequency: Once, reassess lungs and perfusion at the end; no automatic repeat bolus
orders.instructions: Reassess breath sounds and work of breathing at the end of the hour.
orders.rationale: Dry mucous membranes, tachycardia and a 3.5 L estimated deficit (usual weight 83.5 kg versus 80.0 kg). One liter in the first hour (not 1-1.5 L/h repeated) because an acute coronary syndrome is likely: avoid volume overload on an ischemic ventricle.

medication.freqKey: Once, reassess lungs and perfusion at the end; no automatic repeat bolus

orders.name: aspirin chewable tablets (ED loading dose)
orders.instructions: Administer 324 mg (4 x 81 mg) Oral Once, chewed.
orders.rationale: ST depression V4-V6 on the 0140 ECG with a suspected acute coronary syndrome and no aspirin allergy.

medication.freqKey: Once, chewed

orders.name: ondansetron (ZOFRAN) injection, as needed
orders.frequency: Every 6 hours as needed for nausea or vomiting, slowly over 2 minutes; check potassium, magnesium and the ECG QTc before any repeat dose
orders.instructions: Administer 4 mg IV Every 6 hours as needed for nausea or vomiting, slowly over 2 minutes; check potassium, magnesium and the ECG QTc before any repeat dose.
orders.rationale: Nausea and vomiting. QT-prolonging: avoid repeating while potassium is low or the QTc is long (the ECG at 0715 had a long QTc with U waves).

medication.freqKey: Every 6 hours as needed for nausea or vomiting, slowly over 2 minutes; check potassium, magnesium and the ECG QTc before any repeat dose

orders.name: insulin regular (HUMULIN R) 100 units in 0.9% sodium chloride 100 mL (1 unit/mL) infusion - DKA
orders.frequency: Continuous (adult DKA protocol); HOLD for K under 3.5
orders.instructions: Regular insulin 100 units in NS to 100 mL (1 unit/mL) on its own pump channel, 8 units/h, NO bolus. Independent two-nurse check of drug, concentration and rate at initiation and every change. POC glucose hourly, including any hold. HOLD at once for K under 3.5, glucose under 70 or urgent deterioration and notify. Restart only when K is 3.5 or higher AND the prescriber confirms. Insulin titration (POC glucose every hour): glucose under 250 with K 3.5 or higher = add 5% dextrose to the carrier and run 0.05 unit/kg/h (4 units/h); then change the rate by 0.5-1 unit/h to keep the glucose 150-200 until DKA resolves. Falling more than 100 mg/dL in an hour or glucose under 150: call the prescriber for a rate review (reduce, do not stop, while ketones persist). Glucose under 100: call at once and recheck in 15 minutes; glucose under 70: hold the insulin, treat with the hypoglycemia order and check every 15 minutes. DKA is resolved ONLY when beta-hydroxybutyrate is under 0.6 AND (venous pH 7.30 or higher OR bicarbonate 18 or higher); a closed anion gap or a normal glucose alone is not enough. Final stop only with the transition order and the glargine overlap.
orders.rationale: 80 kg x 0.1 unit/kg/h = 8 units/h; no bolus. Started at 0215 after the first potassium (5.2, above 3.5) was known. When the glucose falls under 250 dextrose is added and the rate drops to 0.05 unit/kg/h = 4 units/h. The infusion is held for any K under 3.5 (insulin drives potassium into cells, and ventricular ectopy in an ischemic heart can become ventricular tachycardia).
nursingConsiderations: Hourly POC glucose; strict I&O; telemetry.
High-alert drug: two-nurse check of drug, concentration, rate and patient.
Stop only by order, after the first subcutaneous basal insulin dose has had its overlap.

medication.importantInfo: Insulin moves potassium into cells: the blood level can fall quickly (5.2 to 4.3 in 2 hours here). Ketones and acid-base decide when insulin stops, not the glucose number.
medication.freqKey: Continuous (adult DKA protocol); HOLD for K under 3.5

mar.dispenseLocation: Central Pharmacy (IV room); premixed DKA insulin bag

orders.name: POTASSIUM SAFETY PROTOCOL: two peripheral IVs; never more than 10 mEq/h from ALL sources; one KCl 10 mEq/100 mL rider at a time with a potassium-free carrier; no 40 mEq/L bags; carrier with KCl 20 mEq/L only when no rider is running; HOLD insulin if K is under 3.5; goal K 4.0-5.0 (acute coronary syndrome); continuous telemetry
orders.instructions: PERIPHERAL POTASSIUM SAFETY PROTOCOL (two peripheral IVs, no central line; acute coronary syndrome, so the goal is K 4.0-5.0): before ANY potassium, confirm urine output of at least 0.5 mL/kg/h (40 mL/h at 80 kg) and review the latest creatinine. TOTAL IV potassium from ALL sources on ALL lines must NEVER exceed 10 mEq per hour. While a KCl rider runs the carrier fluid must be POTASSIUM-FREE: swap the 20 mEq/L bag for the plain carrier BEFORE the rider starts (the 20 mEq/L carrier gives 3 mEq/h at 150 mL/h) and put the 20 mEq/L carrier back only after the last rider. Riders are premixed KCl 10 mEq in 100 mL over 1 hour on a pump, ONE at a time, never in parallel, never IV push; no 40 mEq/L bags (central-line strength). K above 5.0 = no potassium, recheck in 2-4 hours. K 4.0-5.0 = carrier with KCl 20 mEq/L. K 3.5-3.9 = two sequential riders (20 mEq) with the potassium-free carrier, then the 20 mEq/L carrier again; recheck after the second. K UNDER 3.5 = HOLD the insulin infusion and notify the prescriber at once; four sequential riders (40 mEq over 4 hours) with the potassium-free carrier; recheck K when the fourth rider ends, drawn from the arm opposite the infusion; restart insulin only when K is 3.5 or higher AND the prescriber confirms (goal 4.0 or higher). Stop replacement and call urgently for an unexpected result, urine under 40 mL/h, a new arrhythmia, extravasation or new pain at the site. Inspect the site and ask about pain every hour during a rider; do not speed the rate. Continuous telemetry throughout.
orders.rationale: Adult DKA protocol: K under 3.5 is replaced before and during insulin; peripheral lines limit the rate to 10 mEq/h.

orders.name: Point-of-care glucose hourly while the insulin infusion is running or temporarily held (begin at 0200), until it is discontinued; the serum glucose is not a substitute. Notify for a fall of more than 100 mg/dL in an hour, glucose under 150, or glucose under 70
orders.instructions: Use the result for the insulin and dextrose steps (see the infusion order).

orders.name: 0.45% sodium chloride 1,000 mL bag, maintenance (ED)
orders.instructions: 200 mL/h by pump through the left forearm IV; reassess volume status and lungs hourly.
orders.rationale: Corrected sodium is normal (138.0), so a hypotonic carrier follows the first liter; 200 mL/h (2.5 mL/kg/h) while the acute coronary syndrome is assessed.

medication.freqKey: Continuous 0245-0500

orders.name: 0.45% sodium chloride + potassium chloride 20 mEq/L, 1,000 mL bag (ED)
orders.frequency: Continuous 0500-0715 (peripheral limit 20 mEq/L; never alongside a KCl rider)
orders.instructions: 150 mL/h by pump through the left forearm IV. The 0700 potassium panel is pending at handoff: change this bag to the potassium-free carrier BEFORE any KCl rider runs.
orders.rationale: K 4.3 (from 5.2) on insulin with an acute coronary syndrome: keep K at 4.0 or higher. Rate cut from 200 to 150 mL/h on cardiology advice (avoid volume overload). 20 mEq/L is the peripheral-line ceiling.

medication.freqKey: Continuous 0500-0715 (peripheral limit 20 mEq/L; never alongside a KCl rider)

orders.name: heparin sodium 4,000 units IV push (ED bolus)
orders.instructions: Independent two-nurse check of the weight-based dose and the cap.
orders.rationale: NSTEMI (hs-troponin I 185 to 640). Weight-based bolus 60 units/kg with the guideline maximum of 4,000 units: 4,800 would exceed it.

medication.dose: 4,000 units (60 units/kg = 4,800, capped at the 4,000-unit maximum)
medication.freqKey: Once

mar.adminDose: 4,000 units (60 units/kg = 4,800, capped at the 4,000-unit maximum)

orders.name: heparin sodium 25,000 units in 250 mL (100 units/mL) infusion - NSTEMI
orders.frequency: Continuous until held at 1030 on Day 2 (cath lab)
orders.instructions: Heparin 25,000 units/250 mL (100 units/mL) at 9.6 mL/h by pump on its OWN IV (right antecubital). Independent two-nurse check at every change. Anti-Xa 6 hours after the start (1130) and about every 6 hours (1900, then 0100 and 0700) and 6 hours after any rate change; adjust only by the pharmacy nomogram when the level is outside 0.30-0.70. CBC with platelets at baseline and daily while on heparin; hold and call for bleeding, platelets under 100 or a 50% fall, or a new neurologic change. Stop at 1030 on Day 2 for transport (cath lab call). Bleeding precautions; no intramuscular injections; no NSAIDs.
orders.rationale: ACS protocol: infusion 12 units/kg/h = 960 units/h at 80 kg (the guideline maximum is 1,000 units/h, so no cap is needed). Anti-Xa target 0.30-0.70 IU/mL. Stopped at 1030 on Day 2 for catheterization (heparin is given in the lab and not resumed after an uncomplicated PCI).
nursingConsiderations: Anti-Xa times are listed in the order; draw from the arm without the infusion.
Watch the right radial puncture site after the catheterization (no heparin running).

medication.importantInfo: A normal bolus-plus-infusion gives a therapeutic anti-Xa within the first sample; check the platelet count for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (days 5-10 is typical, but a baseline and daily counts are the rule).
medication.freqKey: Continuous until held at 1030 on Day 2 (cath lab)

orders.name: atorvastatin (LIPITOR) tablet (ED loading dose, then nightly)
orders.frequency: Once in the ED at 0500, then once daily at 2100 starting Day 2 (no second dose on Day 1)
orders.instructions: Administer 80 mg Oral Once in the ED at 0500, then once daily at 2100 starting Day 2 (no second dose on Day 1).
orders.rationale: NSTEMI: high-intensity statin (LDL 162). The ED dose counts as the Day 1 dose; the nightly 80 mg doses begin at 2100 on Day 2 so two 80 mg doses do not land 16 hours apart.

medication.freqKey: Once in the ED at 0500, then once daily at 2100 starting Day 2 (no second dose on Day 1)

orders.name: Cardiology consultation (urgent NSTEMI management and coronary angiography planning; telephone recommendations at 0500) and Endocrinology consultation (type 1 diabetes, DKA management and transition)
NPO except ice chips while nauseated and while the diagnosis is made

Admit to the Cardiac Step-Down Unit (telemetry bed): DKA precipitated by NSTEMI. Full code. Attending: F. Pelletier, MD (days) / E. Bouchard, MD (nights); cardiology L. Vitale, MD; endocrinology I. Ashcroft, MD

K 3.3 (0655 specimen, released 0710): HOLD the insulin infusion NOW and notify the prescriber. Replace the 0.45% NaCl + KCl 20 mEq/L bag with potassium-free D5 0.45% NaCl at 50 mL/h (glucose 235, under 250), THEN start four sequential KCl 10 mEq/100 mL riders at 0715, 0815, 0915 and 1015 on a pump, one at a time. STAT ECG now. Draw BMP, venous gas, BHB, magnesium, phosphorus, hs-troponin I and anti-Xa when the fourth rider ends (1115), from the arm opposite the infusion. No insulin restart until a repeat K is 3.5 or higher AND the prescriber has reviewed it
orders.instructions: Independent check of the new pump settings. Do not accelerate the potassium. Inspect the peripheral site and ask about pain every hour. Persistent ketosis (BHB 2.6) while insulin is held: the hold is for potassium safety and is as short as possible; the goal is K 4.0 or higher for the ischemic heart.

orders.name: potassium chloride 10 mEq in 100 mL premixed piggyback (riders 1-4)
orders.frequency: Four sequential riders, 0715, 0815, 0915 and 1015, one at a time on a pump; 10 mEq/h maximum from all sources
orders.instructions: Peripheral IV A (left forearm 18 g), pump, ONE bag at a time, never in parallel, never IV push. The carrier must already be potassium-free (D5 0.45% NaCl, no added KCl). Recheck K when the fourth rider ends. Stop and call for pain, redness or swelling, urine under 40 mL/h, an arrhythmia or a new ECG change.
orders.rationale: K 3.3 with frequent unifocal PVCs on insulin in an ischemic myocardium: replace now and keep K at 4.0 or higher. Urine output is adequate (1,350 mL in the ED). The carrier fluid is POTASSIUM-FREE during the four riders, so the combined delivery is exactly 10 mEq/h.

medication.freqKey: Four sequential riders, 0715, 0815, 0915 and 1015, one at a time on a pump; 10 mEq/h maximum from all sources

orders.name: dextrose 5% in 0.45% sodium chloride (no potassium), 1,000 mL bag, carrier during the potassium riders
orders.instructions: 50 mL/h by pump through IV A. Swap the potassium-containing bag out BEFORE the first rider starts. Stays potassium-free until the recheck potassium is back (1130).
orders.rationale: Glucose 235 (under 250) so dextrose is added, but this bag carries NO potassium: the riders supply the potassium (10 mEq/h), so no minute exceeds the peripheral limit. 50 mL/h plus 100 mL/h of rider volume = 150 mL/h total, the rate cardiology set as the ceiling for an ischemic ventricle. Insulin is held, so the 2.5 g/h of dextrose is small.

medication.freqKey: Continuous 0715-1130 during four riders

orders.name: Continuous telemetry with ST-segment monitoring. NOTIFY for chest or epigastric pain, new ST depression, ventricular ectopy (more than 6 per minute, couplets or runs), urine under 40 mL/h for 2 hours, new crackles or oxygen need, bleeding, or any infusion-site injury. Total fluid ceiling today: 150 mL/h of IV fluid including piggybacks unless cardiology changes it. Strict I&O and daily weight
orders.instructions: Peaked T = high K; flat T with U waves = low K, but a normal tracing does not exclude a dangerous level.

orders.name: ECG 12-lead now for frequent PVCs with flat T waves and U waves (K 3.3); acquire 0715, interpretation released 0725
Activity: bedrest with bedside commode on Day 1 (ST depression, heparin infusion, potassium of 3.3); advance to chair and walking in the room on the morning of Day 2 before the catheterization
orders.instructions: Stop and call for chest pressure, dizziness or palpitations with any activity.

orders.name: Sugar-free clear liquids as tolerated (nausea has resolved); no solid food until the DKA resolves. Count every oral volume on the I&O

Cardiology: invasive strategy booked for the morning of Day 2 (coronary angiography with possible PCI, right radial approach, 1100). Endocrinology: follows through discharge. Chemistry, venous gas, BHB, magnesium, phosphorus at 1115 (with hs-troponin I and anti-Xa; draw from the arm opposite the infusion), 1530 and 1850 on Day 1; BMP, magnesium, phosphorus, hs-troponin I and anti-Xa at 0700 on Day 2 (CBC with platelets); BMP and hs-troponin I at 1845 on Day 2; BMP, hs-troponin I, phosphorus and magnesium at 0645 on Day 3 and Day 4 (CBC each morning). orders.name: K 4.1 (1115 specimen, released 1130): the prescriber has reviewed it. stickyNotes.title: Potassium: peripheral IVs, 10 mEq/h limit
stickyNotes.body: Two peripheral IVs, no central line. TOTAL potassium from ALL sources never more than 10 mEq per hour: the 20 mEq/L carrier (3 mEq/h at 150 mL/h) is swapped for a potassium-free carrier BEFORE a KCl rider runs and returns only after the last rider. No 40 mEq/L bags. K under 3.5: HOLD insulin, call, then KCl 10 mEq/100 mL over 1 hour ONE bag at a time (up to four), urine at least 40 mL/h. Goal K 4.0-5.0 for the heart. Peaked T = high K; flat T + U waves + PVCs = low K; a normal tracing does not exclude either.

stickyNotes.title: Insulin (80 kg) and the resolution rule
stickyNotes.body: 8 units/h (0.1 unit/kg/h), no bolus; 4 units/h (0.05 unit/kg/h) with D5 once glucose is under 250 and K 3.5 or higher; goal glucose 150-200. DKA is over only with BHB under 0.6 AND (venous pH 7.30 or higher OR bicarbonate 18 or higher). Basal glargine goes in 2 hours BEFORE the drip stops. Never skip basal insulin, even when NPO.

stickyNotes.title: Heparin (NSTEMI) and the right radial site
stickyNotes.body: Bolus 4,000 units (cap) then 960 units/h (12 units/kg/h) = 9.6 mL/h of 100 units/mL. Anti-Xa 0.30-0.70, checked about every 6 h. Held at 1030 on Day 2 for the cath lab; not resumed. After the catheterization: right arm no cuff, no venipuncture, no lifting over 5 lb. Aspirin plus ticagrelor means easy bruising and bleeding at the radial site.

stickyNotes.title: Chest pain rule
stickyNotes.body: Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL only if systolic BP is 100 or higher and no sildenafil or tadalafil in 48 hours. First episode: STAT ECG within 10 minutes, call cardiology. No relief 5 minutes after the first dose: rapid response. Diabetes can make an MI feel like indigestion: epigastric discomfort counts.

stickyNotes.title: Beta-blocker and low glucose
stickyNotes.body: Metoprolol: check heart rate and blood pressure first; hold for HR under 55 or SBP under 100. It can hide the racing heart of a low glucose; sweating still shows. Glucose under 70: 15 g carbohydrate, recheck in 15 minutes.

stickyNotes.title: Insulin held for K 3.3
stickyNotes.body: Insulin infusion held at 0715. Potassium-free D5 0.45% NaCl 50 mL/h carrier and hourly glucose continue. Four KCl 10 mEq/100 mL riders one at a time; K when the fourth ends; restart only when K is 3.5 or higher AND the prescriber confirms.

stickyNotes.title: Transition (1930)
stickyNotes.body: Glargine 22 units and lispro 6 units at 1930 with dinner; IV insulin (2 units/h) and the carrier run until 2130 (2-hour overlap) after the glargine dose is verified. POC at 2130 and 0300. Metoprolol 12.5 mg due 2000 after HR and BP.

stickyNotes.title: Radial hematoma
stickyNotes.body: Right radial hematoma 1.5 cm at 1900 on Day 2: firm pressure 15 minutes, borders marked, splint until 2300, neurovascular checks; antiplatelets continue. No lifting, pushing up or reaching with the right arm.

stickyNotes.title: Lisinopril: intolerance (dry cough)
stickyNotes.body: Not a true allergy (no angioedema). The reason for losartan instead of an ACE inhibitor. Keep it on the intolerance list.

notes.title: 12-Lead ECG
notes.author: G. Marsh, MD
notes.summary: Sinus tachycardia 114, PR 148 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 432 ms (Bazett), axis +35. Horizontal ST depression 1.5 mm in V4-V6 (0.5 mm in I and aVL, 0.5 mm downsloping in V3) with T-wave inversion V5-V6; no ST elevation (0.5 mm reciprocal change in aVR). Lateral subendocardial ischemia pattern.
notes.body:
**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 114 bpm. PR 148 ms. QRS 88 ms. QTc 432 ms (Bazett). Axis +35 degrees.

**Interpretation**
Sinus tachycardia, regular, no ectopy. Inferior leads: isoelectric ST, normal T waves, no pathological Q waves. V1-V3: normal R-wave progression, isoelectric ST in V1-V2 and a subtle 0.5 mm downsloping ST depression in V3. **V4-V6, I and aVL: 1.5 mm horizontal ST depression in V4, V5 and V6 (0.5 mm in I and aVL) with symmetric T-wave inversion in V5-V6**: acute subendocardial lateral-wall ischemia in the first obtuse marginal territory. No ST elevation in any lead (0.5 mm benign reciprocal change in aVR).

**Context**
Epigastric ache with sweating and fatigue for 36 hours, deep breathing, glucose HIGH on the meter; labs and the first troponin are pending. This is an NSTE-ACS pattern: aspirin given, serial troponin and cardiology to follow.

notes.title: ED Provider Note - Epigastric Ache, Possible DKA and ACS
notes.author: G. Marsh, MD
notes.summary: Deep-breathing, dehydrated 45-year-old with type 1 diabetes, 36 hours of epigastric ache with fatigue and sweating, then vomiting. POC glucose HIGH. The 12-lead ECG (0140) shows 1.5 mm horizontal ST depression V4-V6: NSTE-ACS pattern. Aspirin 324 mg given, 1,000 mL saline started, labs sent, insulin to start once the potassium is known.
notes.body:
**HPI**
45-year-old man with type 1 diabetes since age 14 (multiple daily injections, HbA1c 8.2% six months ago), dyslipidemia and a 25 pack-year smoking history. Thirty-six hours ago, finishing his bus route, he developed a dull, persistent epigastric ache with unusual heavy fatigue and some sweating; he attributed it to indigestion (six calcium carbonate tablets without relief). Yesterday morning he was nauseated and not eating, skipped his mealtime lispro (he believed insulin without food is dangerous) and his bedtime glargine 24 units, and by 2330 had two bilious vomits, polyuria and intense thirst. At 0100 his wife Grace noticed deep, fast breathing and a fruity odor and drove him in. Father died of a STEMI at 48.

**Medicines and allergies**
Glargine 24 units at 2100 (last taken two nights ago), lispro 6 units with meals plus 1 unit per 50 mg/dL over 150 (held 18 hours), atorvastatin 20 mg at bedtime (misses 3-4 doses a week), calcium carbonate as needed. No drug, food or iodinated contrast allergy. **Lisinopril: intolerance (persistent dry cough), not an allergy.**

**Exam**
Anxious, clutching his upper abdomen; deep Kussmaul respirations 26/min; dry mucous membranes; skin warm and flushed; lungs clear; no JVD or edema. Triage vitals: heart rate 114, BP 148/92, SpO2 97% on room air, temperature 98.2 F. POC glucose HIGH. Alert, oriented x4.

**ECG (acquired 0140, read 0150)**
Sinus tachycardia 114 with 1.5 mm horizontal ST depression in V4-V6 (0.5 mm in I and aVL) and T-wave inversion V5-V6. No ST elevation. This is an NSTE-ACS pattern: a "silent" ischemic event in a man with long-standing diabetes (autonomic neuropathy blunts pain) may be the trigger for the ketoacidosis.

**Plan**
Aspirin 324 mg chewed (given 0145). 0.9% sodium chloride 1,000 mL over 1 hour, not more: an ischemic ventricle limits volume. Ondansetron 4 mg IV. VBG, BMP, magnesium, phosphorus, BHB, hs-troponin I, CBC, hepatic and lipid panels, HbA1c and urinalysis are collected; results are pending. Insulin infusion at 0.1 unit/kg/h (8 units/h at 80 kg) without a bolus once the potassium is known to be above 3.5. Continuous telemetry. Cardiology and endocrinology will be called with the results.

notes.title: ED Provider Note - Diagnostic Update, DKA with NSTEMI
notes.author: G. Marsh, MD
notes.summary: Labs released 0210: glucose 540, bicarbonate 12, gap 24, BHB 5.8, venous pH 7.21, K 5.2, creatinine 1.35, hs-troponin I 185 (normal under 14). DKA precipitated by an NSTEMI. Insulin 8 units/h from 0215 with no bolus; potassium held for now; cardiology and endocrinology called.
notes.body:
**Data (released 0210)**
Glucose 540, sodium 131 (corrected for glucose 138.0), potassium 5.2, chloride 95, bicarbonate 12, **anion gap 24**, venous pH 7.21 (pCO2 27; Winter's formula expects 26 +/- 2, so the respiratory compensation is appropriate), beta-hydroxybutyrate 5.8, BUN 28, creatinine 1.35, phosphorus 4.2, magnesium 2.1. **hs-troponin I 185 ng/L** (normal under 14). CBC: WBC 13.8, Hgb 15.6, platelets 265. HbA1c 8.9%. Total cholesterol 248, LDL 162, HDL 34, triglycerides 260. Urinalysis: glucose 4+, ketones 3+, nitrite and leukocyte esterase negative.

**Assessment**
Moderate-to-severe DKA (glucose over 200, BHB over 3.0, pH under 7.3, bicarbonate under 18) precipitated by an acute NSTEMI: the stress-hormone surge from the ischemia plus insulin omission. Corrected sodium 138.0 is normal, so after the first liter a hypotonic carrier (0.45% sodium chloride) is appropriate.

**Plan**
1. Insulin: regular insulin infusion 0.1 unit/kg/h = 8 units/h, no bolus, started at 0215 after the potassium of 5.2 (above 3.5) was known. Hourly point-of-care glucose; goal fall 50-75 mg/dL per hour.
2. Potassium: 5.2 is above 5.0, so none yet; repeat at 0430 and add potassium once it is under 5.0 (goal 4.0-5.0 for the ischemic heart; peripheral IV maximum 10 mEq/h).
3. Fluids: the 1,000 mL bolus finishes at 0245, then 0.45% sodium chloride at 200 mL/h while the volume status and lungs are reassessed.
4. NSTEMI: aspirin given; repeat hs-troponin I with the 0430 draw; calling cardiology now about heparin and the invasive timing; endocrinology for the transition plan.
5. Admit to the Cardiac Step-Down Unit after the repeat labs and metabolic stabilization.

notes.title: ED Provider Note - Repeat Labs, Troponin Rise, Heparin and Potassium Added
notes.author: G. Marsh, MD
notes.summary: Repeat labs (0430): K 4.3 (from 5.2), gap 22, pH 7.25, hs-troponin I 640: dynamic NSTEMI. Cardiology by telephone: heparin bolus 4,000 units (the 4,800 weight-based dose capped at the maximum) and 960 units/h, atorvastatin 80 mg, beta-blocker deferred. Fluid changed to 0.45% NaCl with KCl 20 mEq/L at 150 mL/h.
notes.body:
**Data (released 0450-0455)**
Glucose 380, sodium 134 (corrected 138.5), **potassium 4.3** (down from 5.2 on insulin), chloride 98, bicarbonate 14, **gap 22**, venous pH 7.25 (pCO2 30; Winter's expects 29 +/- 2), BHB 4.2, creatinine 1.25, **hs-troponin I 640 ng/L** (185 at 0140): a rise that confirms a dynamic NSTEMI. Glucose has fallen about 55 mg/dL per hour (540, 505, 450, 395 at 0400).

**Cardiology (telephone, 0500)**
Start unfractionated heparin for NSTEMI at 60 units/kg bolus with a maximum of 4,000 units (80 kg x 60 = 4,800, so 4,000 units) and 12 units/kg/h with a maximum of 1,000 units/h (960 units/h; 100 units/mL bag at 9.6 mL/h), anti-Xa 0.30-0.70 checked 6 hours after the start. Atorvastatin 80 mg. **Oral beta-blocker deferred** until the tachycardia and volume depletion from DKA resolve. Aspirin already given. The P2Y12 inhibitor load waits for the coronary anatomy. Early invasive strategy to be arranged by the cardiology team.

**Done**
Heparin bolus 4,000 units IV and infusion 960 units/h started at 0500 on its own IV; atorvastatin 80 mg at 0500. Because K is 4.3 and falling and must stay at 4.0 or higher with an acute coronary syndrome, the carrier was changed to 0.45% sodium chloride with potassium chloride 20 mEq/L at 150 mL/h (3 mEq/h; below the peripheral maximum of 20 mEq/L in a bag and 10 mEq/h), reduced from 200 mL/h on cardiology advice to limit volume.

**Disposition**
Admission to the Cardiac Step-Down Unit at 0700. The next panel is due at 0655.

notes.title: ED Nursing Note - Reassessment Before Transfer
notes.author: O. Linton, RN
notes.summary: Monitored in resuscitation bay 3 since 0130 for DKA with an acute NSTEMI. Insulin 8 units/h since 0215 (glucose 505 to 285), heparin 960 units/h since 0500, potassium-containing fluid at 150 mL/h. Epigastric ache 1/10, nausea gone, urine 1,350 mL.
notes.body:
Samuel has been on continuous telemetry and pulse oximetry in resuscitation bay 3 since 0130. After the 1,000 mL 0.9% sodium chloride bolus finished at 0245, the maintenance fluid became 0.45% sodium chloride at 200 mL/h. Point-of-care glucose read HIGH at 0130 and has fallen steadily on the insulin infusion: 505 at 0200, 450 at 0300, 395 at 0400, 340 at 0500 and 285 at 0600 (about 55 mg/dL per hour, on target). The 0430 panel showed the anion gap narrowing from 24 to 22 (sodium 134, chloride 98, bicarbonate 14), venous pH 7.25, and potassium falling from 5.2 to 4.3 on the insulin, while the hs-troponin I rose from 185 to 640 ng/L.

Per cardiology recommendations at 0500 he received a heparin IV bolus of 4,000 units (60 units/kg would be 4,800, so the 4,000-unit maximum was given after an independent check) and the infusion is running at 960 units/h (12 units/kg/h, 9.6 mL/h) through the right antecubital 18 gauge IV alone, plus atorvastatin 80 mg by mouth. At 0500 the left forearm fluid was changed to 0.45% sodium chloride with potassium chloride 20 mEq/L at a reduced 150 mL/h to hold the potassium at 4.0 or higher and limit volume on the ischemic heart. The epigastric ache has improved from 4/10 to 1/10; he has not vomited since 0135 (150 mL) and has voided 1,350 mL by urinal since 0200. His wife Grace is at the bedside. Report is going to the Cardiac Step-Down nurse and transport is being arranged for 0700.

notes.title: ED to Cardiac Step-Down Handoff (SBAR)
notes.author: O. Linton, RN
notes.summary: SBAR for transfer: DKA with NSTEMI on insulin 8 units/h, heparin 960 units/h and 0.45% NaCl with KCl 20 mEq/L at 150 mL/h. Two peripheral IVs, no central line. ED totals 0130-0700: intake 1,883 mL, output 1,500 mL (net +383 mL), not to be added to the new shift. Occasional PVCs becoming more frequent; the 0655 panel is collected and not yet resulted.
notes.body:
**Situation**
Samuel Okafor, 45, type 1 diabetes with DKA and an acute NSTEMI, transferring to the Cardiac Step-Down Unit at 0700 on a regular insulin infusion, a heparin infusion and 0.45% sodium chloride with potassium chloride 20 mEq/L. Continuous telemetry; hourly glucose checks.

**Background**
Thirty-six hours of epigastric ache and fatigue, then nausea, vomiting and deep breathing; he skipped his mealtime insulin and his bedtime glargine because he was not eating. ED course: 1,000 mL 0.9% sodium chloride 0145-0245, aspirin 324 mg at 0145, ondansetron 4 mg at 0145, regular insulin 8 units/h from 0215 (no bolus), heparin 4,000 unit bolus and 960 units/h from 0500, atorvastatin 80 mg at 0500. Potassium 5.2 at 0140, 4.3 at 0430. Allergies: none to drugs, food or contrast; lisinopril intolerance (dry cough). Two 18 gauge peripheral IVs: left forearm (carrier fluid and insulin) and right antecubital (heparin alone). ED totals 0130-0700: IV fluid 1,750 mL, IV medicine 83 mL, oral 50 mL = intake 1,883 mL; urine 1,350 mL and emesis 150 mL = output 1,500 mL; net +383 mL. These ED totals are NOT added again to shift 1.

**Assessment**
Epigastric ache 1/10, nausea resolved, lungs clear. Over the last 15 minutes the monitor shows PVCs, occasional and becoming more frequent. The 0655 panel (BMP, venous gas, BHB, magnesium, phosphorus) is collected and not yet resulted; the last potassium was 4.3 and falling on insulin; the glucose at 0600 was 285.

**Recommendation**
Check the 0655 potassium as soon as it releases and look at the monitor now; call the provider at once for a potassium under 3.5 or more ectopy (the potassium protocol is in the orders). Heparin runs on its own IV; check the pumps with the receiving nurse. Hourly glucose; heparin anti-Xa is due at 1130. Next ECG if the ectopy increases.

notes.title: 12-Lead ECG
notes.author: W. Haldane, MD
notes.summary: Sinus rhythm 96 with frequent unifocal ventricular premature beats (left ventricular origin, right bundle branch block pattern, QRS 136 ms; about 7 per minute with couplets and trigeminal runs) near the end of the T-U wave. PR 164 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 492 ms (T-U fusion). Diffuse T-wave flattening with prominent U waves; persistent 1.0 mm ST depression V4-V6. Hypokalemia pattern (potassium 3.3) on top of lateral ischemia.
notes.body:
**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 96 bpm. PR 164 ms. QRS 92 ms (136 ms on the premature beats). QTc 492 ms (Bazett; the T and U waves are fused, so this is a QTc/QUc). Axis +30 degrees.

**Interpretation**
Sinus rhythm with **frequent unifocal ventricular premature beats** (left ventricular origin, right bundle branch block morphology; about 7 per minute, with couplets and trigeminal runs) that fall near the end of the T-U wave: R-on-T risk. Inferior leads: diffuse T-wave flattening with U waves visible after the T in lead II. V1-V3: markedly flattened T waves with **prominent upright U waves (over 1.5 mm in V2-V3, taller than the T wave)**. V4-V6, I and aVL: persistent 1.0 mm horizontal ST depression, flattened T waves, U waves in V4-V5. Compared with 0140: rate slower (114 to 96), ST depression smaller (1.5 to 1.0 mm), new U waves and ventricular ectopy.

**Context**
Potassium 3.3 on the 0655 specimen (released 0710) on an insulin infusion in an acute NSTEMI. Ventricular ectopy on an ischemic myocardium with hypokalemia can degenerate into polymorphic ventricular tachycardia: hold the insulin, replace potassium (peripheral limit 10 mEq/h), keep K at 4.0 or higher and magnesium normal, and keep him on telemetry.

notes.title: Cardiac Step-Down Admission History and Physical
notes.author: F. Pelletier, MD
notes.summary: DKA precipitated by an NSTEMI. On arrival frequent unifocal PVCs; K 3.3 released 0710: insulin held, potassium-free D5 0.45% NaCl at 50 mL/h, four KCl 10 mEq/100 mL riders one at a time (0715-1115), ECG 0715 (flat T, U waves, 1.0 mm ST depression), restart insulin at 4 units/h only at K 3.5 or higher with my confirmation. Heparin 960 units/h; fluids capped at 150 mL/h total; aspirin given; cardiology to see.
notes.body:
**Chief complaint**
Epigastric ache, fatigue, vomiting and deep breathing; admitted from the ED with DKA and an NSTEMI.

**HPI**
See the ED notes. 45-year-old man, type 1 diabetes since 14, who developed a dull epigastric ache with fatigue and sweating about 36 hours before arrival (a "silent" presentation: autonomic neuropathy blunts ischemic pain) and then skipped his lispro and his bedtime glargine because of nausea. ED: glucose 540, bicarbonate 12, gap 24, BHB 5.8, venous pH 7.21, K 5.2, hs-troponin I 185 then 640 ng/L; ECG with 1.5 mm ST depression V4-V6. Treated with 1,000 mL 0.9% saline, aspirin 324 mg, regular insulin 8 units/h from 0215, heparin (4,000 unit bolus, 960 units/h) and atorvastatin 80 mg from 0500, and 0.45% saline with KCl 20 mEq/L at 150 mL/h. On arrival at 0700 his epigastric ache is 1/10 and he is tired with a dry mouth and mild calf cramps.

**PMH, medicines, social, family**
Type 1 diabetes (HbA1c 8.9%; 8.2% six months ago; no DKA in 10 years), dyslipidemia, mild non-proliferative retinopathy, GERD (self-treated). Home: glargine 24 units at 2100, lispro 6 units with meals plus correction, atorvastatin 20 mg (misses doses), calcium carbonate as needed (stop). **Allergies: none to drugs, food or contrast; lisinopril intolerance (dry cough).** Married to Grace (teacher; emergency contact); daughter Naomi (12) and son David (9); city bus driver for 11 years with a commercial driver license; he is frightened that this will cost him his license and income. Smokes 1 pack/day for 25 years. Alcohol 1-2 beers on weekends. Father died of a STEMI at 48; mother 71 with hypertension; paternal uncle CABG at 52.

**Exam (0700-0735)**
Heart rate 96, BP 134/82, respirations 20, SpO2 98% on room air, temperature 98.2 F. Tired, mildly dry mucosa, lungs clear, no JVD or edema, abdomen soft. **Telemetry: sinus rhythm with frequent unifocal PVCs (6 to 8 per minute), flattened T waves, prominent U waves and 1.0 mm ST depression V4-V6.** Weight 80.0 kg (usual dry weight 83.5 kg: about a 3.5 L deficit).

**Data**
0655 panel (released 0710): glucose 235, sodium 136, **potassium 3.3 (critical)**, chloride 103, bicarbonate 16, gap 17, venous pH 7.29, BHB 2.6, creatinine 1.15, magnesium 1.8, phosphorus 2.6. ECG 0715: sinus rhythm 96 with frequent unifocal PVCs, flat T and prominent U waves, QTc 492 ms with T-U fusion, ST depression 1.0 mm V4-V6.

**Assessment and plan**
1. **DKA, improving, with insulin-induced hypokalemia (K 3.3) and ventricular ectopy in an ischemic heart.** Insulin drives potassium into cells: K fell from 5.2 to 3.3 in 5 hours. Orders written: HOLD the insulin infusion now; replace the 0.45% NaCl + KCl 20 mEq/L bag with potassium-free D5 0.45% NaCl at 50 mL/h (glucose 235, under 250); then four sequential KCl 10 mEq/100 mL riders over 1 hour each (0715-1115, one at a time, 10 mEq/h maximum on a peripheral IV, urine output adequate). **While a rider runs the carrier carries no potassium**, so the total never exceeds 10 mEq/h. Draw BMP, gas, BHB, magnesium, phosphorus, troponin and anti-Xa when the fourth rider ends (about 1115, opposite arm). Restart insulin at 0.05 unit/kg/h (4 units/h) with the potassium-containing carrier only when K is 3.5 or higher AND I have reviewed it; the goal K is 4.0 or higher. DKA resolution requires BHB under 0.6 and venous pH 7.30 or higher or bicarbonate 18 or higher.
2. **NSTEMI.** Aspirin given; heparin 960 units/h by anti-Xa (0.30-0.70; first level at 1130); atorvastatin 80 mg given. Beta-blocker deferred by cardiology. Cardiology to consult this morning; an early invasive strategy is expected. NPO status for the procedure to be set by cardiology; for now sugar-free clear liquids. Total IV fluid ceiling 150 mL/h including piggybacks (cardiology). Nitroglycerin and chest-pain orders to follow cardiology. Telemetry with ST monitoring; bedrest with commode.
3. **Fluids and volume.** Estimated deficit 3.5 L; replace slowly because of the ischemic ventricle; lungs and urine every 2 hours.
4. **Tobacco use.** Nicotine withdrawal will start; replacement to be discussed with cardiology.
5. **VTE prevention.** He is on therapeutic heparin now, then dual antiplatelet therapy and early walking: no additional prophylactic anticoagulant is needed.
6. **Home medicines.** Stop calcium carbonate (the "heartburn" was ischemia); atorvastatin 20 mg to be replaced by 80 mg; glargine and lispro to be re-ordered at the transition; lisinopril intolerance noted (an ARB would be the choice later).
7. **Code status** Full code. Wife Grace updated at the bedside; consults: cardiology, endocrinology, dietitian, case management and tobacco treatment to follow.

notes.title: Endocrinology Consultation - DKA with Hypokalemia on Insulin
notes.author: I. Ashcroft, MD
notes.summary: DKA triggered by an NSTEMI plus insulin omission. K 3.3 with PVCs: insulin held, riders in progress. Restart at 4 units/h only at K 3.5 or higher (goal 4.0 or higher) with dextrose; resolution needs BHB under 0.6 plus pH 7.30 or bicarbonate 18; glargine 22 units 2 hours before the drip stops.
notes.body:
I saw Samuel at the bedside for DKA in a 45-year-old man with type 1 diabetes since age 14 (admission HbA1c 8.9%). The history shows a dual trigger: an acute NSTEMI two days ago that presented only as epigastric discomfort and fatigue because of diabetic autonomic neuropathy, driving a surge of epinephrine, glucagon and cortisol; and omission of both his mealtime lispro and his basal glargine (24 units) because he was nauseated and believed that insulin without food is dangerous.

Two points drive this morning's care. First, **dextrose is added once the glucose is under 250** (235 at 0700) so the ketones can clear without a fall in glucose. Second, **insulin lowers potassium**: it fell from 5.2 to 3.3 overnight with frequent PVCs, and the infusion is rightly held. The four sequential peripheral KCl 10 mEq/100 mL riders (0715-1115) run with a **potassium-free** D5 0.45% saline carrier, so the total stays at or under 10 mEq/h. In an ischemic heart the potassium should be 4.0 or higher.

**Plan**
1. When the repeat K at about 1115 is 3.5 or higher (ideally 4.0 or higher) and the covering physician agrees, restart regular insulin at **0.05 unit/kg/h = 4 units/h** with D5 0.45% saline plus KCl 20 mEq/L at 150 mL/h to hold the glucose at 150-200 while the acidosis clears.
2. **Resolution:** BHB under 0.6 mmol/L AND (venous pH 7.30 or higher or bicarbonate 18 or higher). A closed anion gap or a normal glucose alone does not end the infusion.
3. When resolved (expected this evening): glargine 22 units subcutaneously (a small reduction from his home 24 units) with the mealtime lispro **two hours before the IV insulin stops** to prevent rebound ketoacidosis.
4. Basal insulin is never omitted in type 1 diabetes, even if he is NPO for the catheterization. I will teach the sick-day rules before discharge.

notes.title: Cardiology Consultation - NSTEMI with DKA
notes.author: L. Vitale, MD
notes.summary: High-risk NSTEMI (troponin 185 to 640, lateral ST depression), diabetes, LDL 162, 25 pack-years, father died at 48. K 3.3 with PVCs now settling during the third potassium rider. Heparin 960 units/h, aspirin, atorvastatin 80 mg; beta-blocker, ARB and ticagrelor load deferred. Catheterization booked 1100 tomorrow; IV fluids at 150 mL/h or less.
notes.body:
Consulted for NSTEMI in a 45-year-old city bus driver with type 1 diabetes, dyslipidemia (LDL 162, HDL 34, triglycerides 260), 25 pack-years of smoking and a strong family history (father fatal STEMI at 48, uncle CABG at 52). He presented with an anginal equivalent (dull epigastric discomfort, sweating, fatigue) that precipitated DKA. hs-troponin I rose from 185 at 0140 to 640 ng/L at 0430 and the admission ECG shows 1.5 mm horizontal ST depression in V4-V6 with T inversion in V5-V6: a high-risk NSTE-ACS (culprit probably the first obtuse marginal territory).

At 0700 he had hypokalemia (K 3.3) with frequent unifocal PVCs and U waves on telemetry; the PVCs are decreasing now that he is receiving the third KCl 10 mEq/100 mL rider. Potassium and magnesium should be kept at 4.0 or higher and 2.0 or higher in an ischemic heart.

**Recommendations**
1. Continue aspirin (324 mg given; 81 mg daily from tomorrow), atorvastatin 80 mg, and unfractionated heparin: 4,000 unit bolus (the weight-based 4,800 exceeds the 4,000-unit cap) and **960 units/h** (12 units/kg/h; the cap is 1,000), anti-Xa 0.30-0.70 about every 6 hours, platelets daily. Hold the infusion at 1030 tomorrow when called to the cath lab.
2. **Early invasive strategy:** coronary angiography with possible PCI by the right radial route at 1100 tomorrow (Day 2). I am holding the P2Y12 inhibitor (ticagrelor) load until the anatomy is known, in case surgical revascularization is better for multivessel diabetic disease.
3. Oral beta-blocker and an ARB are deferred this morning: he is still volume-depleted and acidotic (pH 7.29, gap 17) and relies on sympathetic tone. Plan low-dose metoprolol once the gap closes and the insulin drip transitions this evening. An ARB (not an ACE inhibitor: lisinopril caused cough) after the catheterization.
4. **IV fluid not above 150 mL/h in total** (piggybacks included) today: a stiff ischemic ventricle can tip into pulmonary edema.
5. Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg sublingual as needed for chest or epigastric pain (systolic BP 100 or higher, no sildenafil or tadalafil in 48 hours) with a STAT ECG and a call to the cardiology fellow for any episode. No NSAIDs.
6. Counsel that smoking is the most modifiable risk; replacement therapy is acceptable after a stable PCI.

notes.title: Pharmacy Note - Anticoagulation, Potassium and Medication Safety Review
notes.author: T. Ng, PharmD
notes.summary: Weight 80.0 kg. Heparin 4,000 unit bolus (capped) and 960 units/h correct; anti-Xa 0.48 therapeutic. Four KCl riders (40 mEq) ran with a potassium-free carrier at 10 mEq/h; K 4.1; insulin restart ordered at 4 units/h. hs-troponin I 1,420 (likely the peak). Lisinopril is a documented intolerance (cough): losartan later.
notes.body:
Reviewed the medication profile, infusion concentrations and labs for Samuel (admission weight 80.0 kg).

**Heparin.** The weight-based bolus is 60 units/kg = 4,800 units but the ACS maximum is 4,000 units: 4,000 units was given. The infusion 12 units/kg/h = 960 units/h (maximum 1,000 units/h) of the 100 units/mL bag = 9.6 mL/h; both are correct as ordered. The 1130 anti-Xa (6 hours after the start) is **0.48 IU/mL**, inside the 0.30-0.70 target: continue 960 units/h unchanged; the next level is at 1900, then about every 6 hours and 6 hours after any change. Baseline platelets 265; daily CBC.

**Potassium.** The four riders (KCl 10 mEq/100 mL over 1 hour, 0715-1115) delivered 40 mEq at exactly 10 mEq/h; the carrier during that time was **D5 0.45% saline with no potassium** at 50 mL/h, so the total never exceeded the peripheral limit of 10 mEq/h (the 20 mEq/L bag resumes only after the last rider). Repeat potassium is **4.1** (released 1130), glucose 242, bicarbonate 17, gap 16, venous pH 7.31, BHB 1.9; the order is to restart regular insulin at 0.05 unit/kg/h = 4 units/h with D5 0.45% saline + KCl 20 mEq/L at 150 mL/h (3 mEq/h). hs-troponin I **1,420 ng/L** (1140), probably the peak.

**Other.** Lisinopril: persistent dry cough is a documented intolerance, not an allergy; when a renin-angiotensin blocker is added after the catheterization, losartan (an ARB) is the right choice with potassium and creatinine checked within a week. Ondansetron is a QT-prolonging drug: avoid repeating it while the QTc is long. Home calcium carbonate should be stopped (the ache was ischemia).

notes.author: A. Vogt, MD

notes.title: Cardiology Fellow Event Note - Recurrent Chest Pressure
notes.author: A. Vogt, MD
notes.summary: New 5/10 retrosternal and epigastric pressure at 1400 with mild shortness of breath; ECG 1405 deeper lateral ST depression (1.5 mm V4-V6); one sublingual nitroglycerin at 1410 relieved it within 4 minutes and the ST changes returned toward baseline. No emergent catheterization; invasive study stays at 1100 tomorrow.
notes.body:
Called to the bedside at 1405 for **new 5/10 dull, squeezing pressure across the lower sternum and epigastrium with mild shortness of breath**, which began at 1400 during a routine glucose check (glucose 208). Heart rate and blood pressure were above his baseline at the first check; the telemetry showed sinus rhythm without PVCs but a transient deepening of ST depression in V5. A STAT 12-lead ECG at 1405 (read 1415) shows **horizontal ST depression of 1.5 mm in V4-V6**, deeper than the 1.0 mm on the 0715 tracing, with T-wave inversion in V5-V6 and no ectopy or U waves (potassium was 4.1 at 1115).

After confirming systolic BP above 100 and no phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor use, **nitroglycerin 0.4 mg sublingual** was given at 1410 per the as-needed order. Within 4 minutes (by 1414) the pressure was gone (0/10), blood pressure and heart rate settled and the V5 depression returned toward its baseline on telemetry.

**Assessment:** recurrent angina from the culprit lateral lesion on a background of NSTEMI, responsive to nitrate, no hemodynamic or rhythm instability, no heart failure signs. **Plan:** continue heparin 960 units/h and aspirin; keep the invasive study at 1100 tomorrow (an emergent transfer is not needed because the pain resolved quickly and the ST changes reversed); the beta-blocker starts once the DKA resolves this evening; repeat hs-troponin I with the 1850 panel; call me for any further episode, more than one nitroglycerin dose needed, hypotension, or new ST elevation. He and his wife were told that the pressure in his upper stomach and lower chest was his heart and not indigestion, and what to do next time.

notes.title: Hospital Medicine Note - Gap Narrowing, Ketones Persist; Chest Pressure at 1400
notes.author: F. Pelletier, MD
notes.summary: DKA improving but NOT resolved: 1530 gap 15, bicarbonate 19, venous pH 7.34, BHB 1.1 (above 0.6), K 4.0 on the 20 mEq/L carrier. Insulin continues at 4 units/h with D5. Chest pressure at 1400 relieved by one nitroglycerin; cardiology saw him.
notes.body:
Panel at 1530 (released 1545): glucose 195, sodium 138, **potassium 4.0**, chloride 104, bicarbonate 19, gap 15, venous pH 7.34, BHB **1.1**, creatinine 1.02, phosphorus 2.7, magnesium 2.0.

**DKA:** better but not resolved. The venous pH is above 7.30 and the bicarbonate is above 18, but the BHB is 1.1 mmol/L (the gate is under 0.6) and the gap is still 15: the insulin infusion continues at 4 units/h with D5 0.45% NaCl + KCl 20 mEq/L at 150 mL/h; glucose is 195-208 on the hourly checks (goal 150-200). Potassium is at the 4.0 goal on the carrier; no extra rider is needed while insulin runs (recheck with the 1850 panel). A venous pH above 7.30 and a bicarbonate above 18 do not by themselves mean the ketones are cleared.

**NSTEMI:** one episode of 5/10 retrosternal pressure at 1400 (see the cardiology fellow's note), relieved by sublingual nitroglycerin; no PVCs since the potassium was corrected. Continue heparin; the next anti-Xa and a repeat hs-troponin I are due with the 1850 draw; beta-blocker after the DKA resolves.

**Fluids:** about 150 mL/h of IV fluid in total; lungs clear; urine adequate. Plan the subcutaneous transition when the BHB is under 0.6 (basal insulin 2 hours before the drip stops).

notes.title: Endocrinology - DKA Resolved, Transition to Subcutaneous Insulin
notes.author: I. Ashcroft, MD
notes.summary: DKA resolved on the 1850 specimen: BHB 0.4, venous pH 7.38, bicarbonate 22, gap 12, glucose 165, K 4.2. Glargine 22 units and lispro 6 units at 1930 with dinner; IV insulin 2 units/h and D5 + KCl carrier until 2130 (2-hour overlap). hs-troponin I 1,280 (down from 1,420); anti-Xa 0.52.
notes.body:
The 1850 specimen (released 1905-1915) shows glucose 165, sodium 139, **potassium 4.2**, chloride 105, bicarbonate 22, **gap 12**, venous pH 7.38 (pCO2 40; Winter's expects 41 +/- 2), **BHB 0.4**, creatinine 0.95, phosphorus 3.0, magnesium 2.1. DKA is resolved: BHB under 0.6 with venous pH 7.30 or higher and bicarbonate 18 or higher. hs-troponin I **1,280** (the peak was 1,420 at 1130) and the anti-Xa is 0.52, therapeutic.

**Transition (orders written 1915):**
- Insulin glargine **22 units** SC at 1930 (0.275 unit/kg; home dose 24) and insulin lispro **6 units** with the consistent-carbohydrate dinner at 1930, with the correction scale before meals (151-200 +1, 201-250 +2, 251-300 +3, over 300 +4 and call).
- **Keep the IV insulin (reduced to 2 units/h) and the D5 0.45% NaCl + KCl 20 mEq/L carrier running until 2130**, a 2-hour overlap: stopping the drip earlier lets ketones rebound before the glargine acts. POC glucose at 2000, 2100, 2130 and 0300.
- No glargine at 2100 tonight (given at 1930); the next dose is 2100 tomorrow.
- Consistent-carbohydrate (60 g per meal), heart-healthy diet from dinner. Basal insulin is never held, including tomorrow while he is NPO for the catheterization (the mealtime dose is held).

notes.title: Night Hospitalist Note - Transition, Beta-Blocker Start, Catheterization Preparation
notes.author: E. Bouchard, MD
notes.summary: Evening rounds after DKA resolution. Subcutaneous insulin given at 1930 with the IV overlap to 2130. Metoprolol tartrate 12.5 mg every 12 hours started at 2000 (HR and BP checked first; hold for HR under 55 or SBP under 100). NPO after midnight except medicines; NS 100 mL/h from 0700 tomorrow; heparin continues, anti-Xa therapeutic.
notes.body:
I reviewed Samuel after the 1900 resolution (glucose 165, pH 7.38, bicarbonate 22, gap 12, BHB 0.4). He is eating the dinner tray without nausea or recurrent epigastric discomfort since the glargine 22 units and lispro 6 units at 1930; the IV insulin continues until 2130 (overlap) per the endocrinology orders.

With the ketoacidosis, osmotic diuresis and volume deficit resolved, an oral beta-blocker is started for the NSTEMI: **metoprolol tartrate 12.5 mg by mouth every 12 hours, first dose at 2000, only after the nurse checks the heart rate and blood pressure; hold for heart rate under 55 or systolic BP under 100.** It can blunt the tachycardia and tremor of a low glucose (sweating is not blocked), so glucose checks continue. Atorvastatin 80 mg was given in the ED at 0500; the next 80 mg dose is at 2100 tomorrow. Heparin continues at 960 units/h; the 1850 anti-Xa was 0.52 and the next is at 0100.

For tomorrow's 1100 catheterization: **NPO except medicines from midnight**, hold the 0730 mealtime lispro while NPO (never the basal), 0.9% sodium chloride at 100 mL/h from 0700 for contrast-kidney protection (creatinine 0.95 now, 1.35 on arrival), heparin held at 1030 on the cath lab call, and aspirin 81 mg and metoprolol with a sip of water at 0800. Ticagrelor is not given before the study.

notes.title: Night Hospitalist Note - Overnight Summary Before Catheterization
notes.author: E. Bouchard, MD
notes.summary: Quiet night after the transition: IV insulin and D5 stopped at 2130, glucose 172, 162, 156 and 146 (0300) on glargine 22 units. No chest or epigastric discomfort, no ectopy. 0100 anti-Xa 0.55 (therapeutic) on heparin 960 units/h. NPO since midnight; 0645 labs drawn.
notes.body:
Overnight course after the evening transition to subcutaneous insulin: glargine 22 units and lispro 6 units at 1930; the IV insulin (2 units/h) and the D5 0.45% saline + KCl 20 mEq/L carrier were stopped at 2130 per the 2-hour overlap order. Point-of-care glucose: 172 at 2000, 162 at 2100, 156 at 2130 and 146 at 0300 (no correction needed, no low). He took metoprolol tartrate 12.5 mg at 2000 and tolerated it, and atorvastatin is next due tonight at 2100. He slept well; telemetry showed sinus rhythm without ectopy and no ischemic ST changes; no chest or epigastric discomfort. The 0100 heparin anti-Xa returned at 0.55 IU/mL (therapeutic) and the infusion continues at 960 units/h through the right antecubital IV. He has been NPO since midnight except medicines. The 0645 labs are drawn and pending.

**For today:** NPO for the 1100 catheterization (sips with medicines); 0.9% sodium chloride 100 mL/h from 0700; hold the 0730 mealtime lispro while NPO but never the basal insulin (the glargine given at 1930 is active; the next dose is at 2100); aspirin 81 mg and metoprolol 12.5 mg with a sip of water at 0800; hold heparin at 1030; right arm: no cuff or venipuncture after the procedure.

notes.title: Endocrinology Progress Note - NPO Insulin Plan, Day 2
notes.author: I. Ashcroft, MD
notes.summary: No rebound ketosis: glucose 142, bicarbonate 24, gap 11, BHB 0.2, K 4.3. Hold the 0730 mealtime lispro while NPO; basal glargine stays on board; glargine 22 units again at 2100 tonight; lispro 6 units plus correction resumes with lunch.
notes.body: Day 2 after the transition to subcutaneous basal-bolus insulin. The 0700 panel shows sustained resolution with no rebound ketosis: glucose 142, sodium 139, potassium 4.3, chloride 104, bicarbonate 24, anion gap 11, BUN 14, creatinine 0.92, **BHB 0.2**. Because he is NPO for the 1100 catheterization, the 0730 mealtime lispro (6 units) is held; no correction is needed since his glucose was 142 (150 or below). Glucose will be checked before he goes to the cath lab (1030) and on return. The key point for the team and for him: a person with type 1 diabetes must always have basal insulin on board, even when NPO, because with no insulin ketones rise within 4 to 6 hours. The glargine 22 units from 1930 last night is active. Once he eats after the procedure he resumes lispro 6 units before meals with the low-dose correction scale, and glargine 22 units is due at 2100 tonight. I will see him on Day 3 for sick-day education.

notes.title: Cardiology Pre-Procedure Note - Coronary Angiography, Possible PCI
notes.author: R. Quintero, MD
notes.summary: Pre-procedure check complete: informed consent (angiography, possible PCI) signed; bilateral radial and ulnar flow documented (modified Allen test normal); creatinine 0.92; contrast volume to be kept small; heparin held at 1030; right radial route. He is worried about his commercial driver license; reassured that case management and cardiology will work on the certification timeline.
notes.body:
Reviewed the indication (NSTEMI, hs-troponin I peak so far 1,420 ng/L, 1.5 mm lateral ST depression, recurrent angina at 1400 yesterday), the risks (bleeding, radial artery occlusion, stroke, contrast kidney injury, myocardial infarction, death) and the alternatives. **Informed consent for coronary angiography and possible PCI is signed and witnessed.** Baseline creatinine 0.92 mg/dL (0700); no contrast or shellfish allergy; he is hydrating with 0.9% saline 100 mL/h since 0700. Right wrist and both groins are prepped; **bilateral radial and ulnar pulses 2+ with a normal modified Allen test (plethysmography)**; radial and pedal pulses marked in ink. Glucose before transport 136 mg/dL (1030). The heparin infusion is held at 1030 for the lab (procedural heparin will be given and not resumed afterwards unless the anatomy requires it). Aspirin 81 mg and metoprolol were taken at 0800. The ticagrelor loading dose will be given after the stent is placed.

Mr. Okafor spent time with me asking whether a stent or his diabetes will cost him his commercial driver license; I told him that this is a medical certification question with a usual waiting period after a heart attack and stent, that we will document his recovery, ejection fraction and an exercise test, and that case management and endocrinology will work through the paperwork with him. He is going to the cath lab at 1040.

notes.title: Cardiac Catheterization and PCI Procedure Note
notes.author: R. Quintero, MD
notes.summary: Right radial coronary angiography with PCI: 90% eccentric thrombotic ulcerated stenosis of the first obtuse marginal (culprit, TIMI-2 flow) treated with a 3.0 x 22 mm zotarolimus-eluting stent, 0% residual, TIMI-3. LAD 30%, RCA 20%, left main normal, LVEDP 11. Contrast 85 mL. Ticagrelor 180 mg at 1215. Radial compression band 14 mL, hemostasis confirmed.
notes.body:
**Procedure:** left heart catheterization, selective coronary angiography and percutaneous coronary intervention with a 3.0 x 22 mm zotarolimus-eluting stent in the first obtuse marginal (OM1) branch of the left circumflex artery, right radial approach.

**Indication:** 45-year-old man with type 1 diabetes and NSTEMI (hs-troponin I peak 1,420 ng/L, V4-V6 ST depression, recurrent angina) that precipitated DKA.

**Sedation and access:** moderate sedation with fentanyl 50 mcg IV and midazolam 1 mg IV. Right radial artery accessed under ultrasound guidance with a 6 French hydrophilic sheath; verapamil 2.5 mg and nitroglycerin 200 mcg given through the sheath for spasm prophylaxis.

**Findings:** left main normal. LAD mild 30% non-obstructive mid plaque. Right coronary dominant with 20% luminal irregularities. Left circumflex gives a large OM1 with a discrete ulcerated **90% eccentric thrombotic stenosis and TIMI-2 flow: the culprit lesion** matching the lateral ST depression. **LVEDP 11 mmHg (normal).**

**Intervention:** therapeutic ACT 285 seconds on procedural unfractionated heparin; 6 French 3.5-curve extra-backup guide in the left main; 0.014-inch wire across the lesion; pre-dilation with a 2.5 x 15 mm balloon; 3.0 x 22 mm drug-eluting stent deployed at 14 atmospheres and post-dilated with a 3.25 mm non-compliant balloon: **0% residual stenosis and brisk TIMI-3 flow.** No complications.

**Contrast and hemostasis:** low-osmolar iohexol 350, total 85 mL (kept low to protect the kidneys; creatinine 0.92 before). **Ticagrelor 180 mg given on the table at 1215** to start dual antiplatelet therapy. The sheath was removed and a radial compression band was applied with 14 mL of air, with patent hemostasis confirmed by plethysmography during ulnar compression.

**Plan:** heparin infusion stays off. Aspirin 81 mg daily and ticagrelor 90 mg every 12 hours (first dose 12 hours after the load, at midnight) for at least 12 months. Continue 0.9% saline 100 mL/h until 1900; creatinine at 1845, at 0645 on Day 3 and on Day 4. Right radial band protocol and neurovascular checks; no cuff, venipuncture or lifting over 5 pounds on the right arm. Echocardiogram tomorrow. High-intensity statin, beta-blocker, and an ARB (losartan; lisinopril caused cough) to be started by the primary team.

notes.title: 12-Lead ECG
notes.author: W. Haldane, MD
notes.summary: Sinus rhythm 68, PR 160 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 418 ms (Bazett), axis +32. Complete resolution of the lateral ST depression in V4-V6; upright T in V4-V5, trace flattening in V6; U waves gone; no premature beats. Compatible with reperfusion of the first obtuse marginal after stenting.
notes.body:
**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 68 bpm. PR 160 ms. QRS 86 ms. QTc 418 ms (Bazett). Axis +32 degrees.

**Interpretation**
Normal sinus rhythm, completely regular, no premature atrial or ventricular beats. Inferior leads: isoelectric ST, normal T. V1-V3: isoelectric ST, normal T-wave amplitude, **U waves gone**. **V4-V6, I and aVL: complete resolution of the horizontal ST depression** (isoelectric), upright T in V4-V5 with only trace flattening in V6. Compared with 1405 yesterday and 0140: resolved.

**Context**
Post drug-eluting stent to the first obtuse marginal (right radial, completed about 1215). Potassium 4.3 at 0700. Telemetry can continue.
notes.impression: Normal sinus rhythm 68. Lateral ST depression resolved, no U waves, no ectopy. QTc 418 ms.
